title_original: ‘Ebenezer’ tops global box office with $42m opening weekend, ‘Ramayana’ nears $150m
excerpt_original: David Leitch’s ‘How To Rob A Bank’ starts in fifth place on global chart.

blocks.text: The Cat In The Hat (Warner Bros)
Credit: Rentrak. All figures are estimates.
Johnny Depp returned to the global box office summit with his starring role in Ti West’s Ebenezer , which started with a $42m weekend worldwide.
Starting in 64 territories for Paramount, the film had a fairly even split between international and domestic, with $23m in the former and $19m in the latter, according to figures from Rentrak.
It topped the charts in UK-Ireland (with $5.4m), Italy (with $2m), Mexico (with $1.7m), Spain, Poland, and Belgium, and took second place in France, Germany, Brazil, the Netherlands, and Colombia.
It is the first film starring Depp to top the charts since Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes Of Grindelwald in November 2018. The actor has since had a career hiatus amid legal issues.

Ebenezer is a comedy-horror retelling of Charles Dickens’ 1843 novella A Christmas Carol , following the miserly businessman Ebenezer Scrooge as he is visited by three ghosts at Christmas. Rupert Grint, Andrea Riseborough, Tramell Tillman, Sam Claflin, Daisy Ridley, Ian McKellen and Ellie Bamber are also in the cast.
Upcoming release territories include India and Sri Lanka from November 20, and the Philippines from December 2.
Bollywood blockbuster Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend is nearing $150m after holding second place globally on its second weekend in cinemas for Sony.

The action title posted a decent -34% hold with $38.1m worldwide, consisting of $32.6m internationally and $5.5m in North America, and is up to $123.4m and $24.1m in each market, according to Rentrak figures.
It has $147.5m combined so far and is playing in 44 territories. New markets this weekend included Mexico, Indonesia and Cambodia, each of which set record openings for an Indian film.
Imax continued to power its release, with $3m worldwide for the weekend, of which $2.6m came from international territories and $1.2m from India alone.
Upcoming territories include Brazil, Italy, Ukraine and Hungary (all November 19), and Argentina, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Central America (all November 26).

Last weekend’s number one Godzilla Minus Zero slipped to fourth place on its second session with a $15.7m weekend and $89.9m total. This broke down as $7.3m from international and $8.3m from North America, with $41m and $48.9m totals, respectively.
It remains the Imax leader, with a $4.8m session and $32m lifetime, almost 29% of its total takings.
Amazon MGM Studios crime comedy How To Rob A Bank was the second-highest-grossing new title of the weekend, taking fifth place in the chart with a slow $10.3m worldwide session.

This consisted of $5.1m from 73 international markets and $5.2m from North America. France led the way internationally with $460,000, with top territories also including Australia ($380,000), Germany ($340,000) and Spain ($335,000). Sony handles international distribution.

Directed by John Wick and Bullet Train director David Leitch, How To Rob A Bank follows a criminal gang who document their heists on social media. Nicholas Hoult, Zoe Kravitz, Pete Davidson, John C. Reilly and Christian Slater lead the cast.
With awards season starting to kick into gear, contending titles in the chart included Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine , in sixth place with a $10m second session for Disney.

The Searchlight Pictures comedy-drama took $5.4m internationally, falling only 28% overall. Top holds came in France (-5%), Greece (-8%), Belgium (-21%), Italy (-24%), and the Netherlands (-25%). The film also opened in Germany and Spain, 7% and 34% ahead of The Banshees Of Inisherin, respectively.
It is up to $28m worldwide, with $14.7m from international and $13.3m domestic, and could still challenge the $52.3m lifetime of Banshees if it continues to hold well.

Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything fell just 16% worldwide. Four new territories, including Australia-New Zealand, boosted its international weekend to $2.2m and $2.3m total, while it is up to $91.3m worldwide thanks to its huge $89m in North America.
The film expands to international markets including UK-Ireland, Greece, Russia, Denmark, Norway, Sweden and Finland this coming weekend.
Laika’s stop-motion animation epic Wildwood put on $6.9m this session, with $3.3m from international.
It is up to $70.1m worldwide, with $21.6m from international markets, with territories to come, including France on December 9.
